ndant experts for the prefilling stage. For each GPU, besides the original 8 experts it hosts, it will also host one additional redundant expert. Furthermore, in the prefilling sta
ge, to improve the throughput and hide the overhead of all-to-all and TP communication, we simultaneously process two micro-batches with similar computational workloads, overlappin
g the attention and MoE of one micro-batch with the dispatch and combine of another. Finally, we are exploring a dynamic redundancy strategy for experts, where each GPU hosts more
experts (e.g., 16 experts), but only 9 will be activated during each inference step. Before the all-to-all operation at each layer begins, we compute the globally optimal routing s
cheme on the fly. Given the substantial computation involved in the prefilling stage, the overhead of computing this routing scheme is almost negligible. 3.4.2 Decoding During deco
ding, we treat the shared expert as a routed one. From this perspective, each token will select 9 experts during routing, where the shared expert is regarded as a heavy-load one th
at will always be selected. The minimum deployment unit of the decoding stage consists of 40 nodes with 320 GPUs. The attention part employs TP4 with SP, combined with DP80, while
the MoE part uses EP320. For the MoE part, each GPU hosts only one expert, and 64 GPUs are responsible for hosting redundant experts and shared experts. All-to-all communication of
the dispatch and combine parts is performed via direct point-to-point transfers over IB to achieve low latency. Additionally, we leverage the IBGDA ( NVIDIA, 2022 ) technology to
further minimize latency and enhance communication efficiency. Similar to prefilling, we periodically determine the set of redundant experts in a certain interval, based on the sta
tistical expert load from our online service. However, we do not need to rearrange experts since each GPU only hosts one expert. We are also exploring the dynamic redundancy strate
gy for decoding. However, this requires more careful optimization of the algorithm that computes the globally optimal routing scheme and the fusion with the dispatch kernel to redu
ce overhead. Additionally, to enhance throughput and hide the overhead of all-to-all communication, we are also exploring processing two micro-batches with similar computational wo
rkloads simultaneously in the decoding stage. Unlike prefilling, attention consumes a larger portion of time in the decoding stage. Therefore, we overlap the attention of one micro
-batch with the dispatch+MoE+combine of another. In the decoding stage, the batch size per expert is relatively small (usually within 256 tokens), and the bottleneck is memory acce
ss rather than computation. Since the MoE part only needs to load the parameters of one expert, the memory access overhead is minimal, so using fewer SMs will not significantly aff
ect the overall performance. Therefore, to avoid impacting the computation speed of the attention part, we can allocate only a small portion of SMs to dispatch+MoE+combine . 3.5 Su
ggestions on Hardware Design Based on our implementation of the all-to-all communication and FP8 training scheme, we propose the following suggestions on chip design to AI hardware
vendors. 3.5.1 Communication Hardware In DeepSeek-V3, we implement the overlap between computation and communication to hide the communication latency during computation. This sig
nificantly reduces the dependency on communication bandwidth compared to serial computation and communication. However, the current communication implementation relies on expensive
SMs (e.g., we allocate 20 out of the 132 SMs available in the H800 GPU for this purpose), which will limit the computational throughput. Moreover, using SMs for communication resu
lts in significant inefficiencies, as tensor cores remain entirely under-utilized. Currently, the SMs primarily perform the following tasks for all-to-all communication: • Forwardi
ng data between the IB (InfiniBand) and NVLink domain while aggregating IB traffic destined for multiple GPUs within the same node from a single GPU. • Transporting data between RD
MA buffers (registered GPU memory regions) and input/output buffers. • Executing reduce operations for all-to-all combine . • Managing fine-grained memory layout during chunked dat
a transferring to multiple experts across the IB and NVLink domain. We aspire to see future vendors developing hardware that offloads these communication tasks from the valuable co
mputation unit SM, serving as a GPU co-processor or a network co-processor like NVIDIA SHARP Graham et al. (2016) . Furthermore, to reduce application programming complexity, we ai
m for this hardware to unify the IB (scale-out) and NVLink (scale-up) networks from the perspective of the computation units. With this unified interface, computation units can eas
ily accomplish operations such as read , write , multicast , and reduce across the entire IB-NVLink-unified domain via submitting communication requests based on simple primitives.
3.5.2 Compute Hardware Higher FP8 GEMM Accumulation Precision in Tensor Cores. In the current Tensor Core implementation of the NVIDIA Hopper architecture, FP8 GEMM suffers from l
imited accumulation precision. After aligning 32 mantissa products by right-shifting based on the maximum exponent, the Tensor Core only uses the highest 14 bits of each mantissa p
roduct for addition, and truncates bits exceeding this range. The accumulation of addition results into registers also employs 14-bit precision. Our implementation partially mitiga
tes the limitation by accumulating the addition results of 128 FP8 FP8 multiplications into registers with FP32 precision in the CUDA core. Although helpful in achieving successful
FP8 training, it is merely a compromise due to the Hopper architecture’s hardware deficiency in FP8 GEMM accumulation precision. Future chips need to adopt higher precision. Suppo
rt for Tile- and Block-Wise Quantization. Current GPUs only support per-tensor quantization, lacking the native support for fine-grained quantization like our tile- and block-wise
quantization. In the current implementation, when the interval is reached, the partial results will be copied from Tensor Cores to CUDA cores, multiplied by the scaling factors, an
d added to FP32 registers on CUDA cores. Although the dequantization overhead is significantly mitigated combined with our precise FP32 accumulation strategy, the frequent data mov
ements between Tensor Cores and CUDA cores still limit the computational efficiency. Therefore, we recommend future chips to support fine-grained quantization by enabling Tensor Co
res to receive scaling factors and implement MMA with group scaling. In this way, the whole partial sum accumulation and dequantization can be completed directly inside Tensor Core
s until the final result is produced, avoiding frequent data movements. Support for Online Quantization. The current implementations struggle to effectively support online quantiza
tion, despite its effectiveness demonstrated in our research. In the existing process, we need to read 128 BF16 activation values (the output of the previous computation) from HBM
(High Bandwidth Memory) for quantization, and the quantized FP8 values are then written back to HBM, only to be read again for MMA. To address this inefficiency, we recommend that
future chips integrate FP8 cast and TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) access into a single fused operation, so quantization can be completed during the transfer of activations from g
lobal memory to shared memory, avoiding frequent memory reads and writes. We also recommend supporting a warp-level cast instruction for speedup, which further facilitates the bett
er fusion of layer normalization and FP8 cast. Alternatively, a near-memory computing approach can be adopted, where compute logic is placed near the HBM. In this case, BF16 elemen
ts can be cast to FP8 directly as they are read from HBM into the GPU, reducing off-chip memory access by roughly 50%. Support for Transposed GEMM Operations. The current architect
ure makes it cumbersome to fuse matrix transposition with GEMM operations. In our workflow, activations during the forward pass are quantized into 1x128 FP8 tiles and stored. Durin
g the backward pass, the matrix needs to be read out, dequantized, transposed, re-quantized into 128x1 tiles, and stored in HBM. To reduce memory operations, we recommend future ch
ips to enable direct transposed reads of matrices from shared memory before MMA operation, for those precisions required in both training and inference. Combined with the fusion of
FP8 format conversion and TMA access, this enhancement will significantly streamline the quantization workflow. 4 Pre-Training 4.1 Data Construction Compared with DeepSeek-V2, we
optimize the pre-training corpus by enhancing the ratio of mathematical and programming samples, while expanding multilingual coverage beyond English and Chinese. Also, our data pr
ocessing pipeline is refined to minimize redundancy while maintaining corpus diversity. Inspired by Ding et al. (2024) , we implement the document packing method for data integrity
but do not incorporate cross-sample attention masking during training. Finally, the training corpus for DeepSeek-V3 consists of 14.8T high-quality and diverse tokens in our tokeni
zer. In the training process of DeepSeekCoder-V2 ( DeepSeek-AI, 2024a ) , we observe that the Fill-in-Middle (FIM) strategy does not compromise the next-token prediction capability
while enabling the model to accurately predict middle text based on contextual cues. In alignment with DeepSeekCoder-V2, we also incorporate the FIM strategy in the pre-training o
f DeepSeek-V3. To be specific, we employ the Prefix-Suffix-Middle (PSM) framework to structure data as follows: This structure is applied at the document level as a part of the pre
-packing process. The FIM strategy is applied at a rate of 0.1, consistent with the PSM framework. The tokenizer for DeepSeek-V3 employs Byte-level BPE ( Shibata et al., 1999 ) wit
h an extended vocabulary of 128K tokens. The pretokenizer and training data for our tokenizer are modified to optimize multilingual compression efficiency. In addition, compared wi
th DeepSeek-V2, the new pretokenizer introduces tokens that combine punctuations and line breaks. However, this trick may introduce the token boundary bias ( Lundberg, 2023 ) when
the model processes multi-line prompts without terminal line breaks, particularly for few-shot evaluation prompts. To address this issue, we randomly split a certain proportion of
such combined tokens during training, which exposes the model to a wider array of special cases and mitigates this bias. 4.2 Hyper-Parameters Model Hyper-Parameters. We set the num
ber of Transformer layers to 61 and the hidden dimension to 7168. All learnable parameters are randomly initialized with a standard deviation of 0.006. In MLA, we set the number of
attention heads to 128 and the per-head dimension to 128. The KV compression dimension is set to 512, and the query compression dimension is set to 1536. For the decoupled queries
and key, we set the per-head dimension to 64. We substitute all FFNs except for the first three layers with MoE layers. Each MoE layer consists of 1 shared expert and 256 routed e
xperts, where the intermediate hidden dimension of each expert is 2048. Among the routed experts, 8 experts will be activated for each token, and each token will be ensured to be s
ent to at most 4 nodes. The multi-token prediction depth is set to 1, i.e., besides the exact next token, each token will predict one additional token. As DeepSeek-V2, DeepSeek-V3
also employs additional RMSNorm layers after the compressed latent vectors, and multiplies additional scaling factors at the width bottlenecks. Under this configuration, DeepSeek-V
3 comprises 671B total parameters, of which 37B are activated for each token. Training Hyper-Parameters. We employ the AdamW optimizer ( Loshchilov and Hutter, 2017 ) with hyper-pa
rameters set to , , and . We set the maximum sequence length to 4K during pre-training, and pre-train DeepSeek-V3 on 14.8T tokens. As for the learning rate scheduling, we first lin
early increase it from 0 to during the first 2K steps. Then, we keep a constant learning rate of until the model consumes 10T training tokens. Subsequently, we gradually decay the
learning rate to in 4.3T tokens, following a cosine decay curve. During the training of the final 500B tokens, we keep a constant learning rate of in the first 333B tokens, and swi
tch to another constant learning rate of in the remaining 167B tokens. The gradient clipping norm is set to 1.0. We employ a batch size scheduling strategy, where the batch size is
gradually increased from 3072 to 15360 in the training of the first 469B tokens, and then keeps 15360 in the remaining training. We leverage pipeline parallelism to deploy differe
nt layers of a model on different GPUs, and for each layer, the routed experts will be uniformly deployed on 64 GPUs belonging to 8 nodes. As for the node-limited routing, each tok
en will be sent to at most 4 nodes (i.e., ). For auxiliary-loss-free load balancing, we set the bias update speed to 0.001 for the first 14.3T tokens, and to 0.0 for the remaining
500B tokens. For the balance loss, we set to 0.0001, just to avoid extreme imbalance within any single sequence. The MTP loss weight is set to 0.3 for the first 10T tokens, and to
0.1 for the remaining 4.8T tokens. Figure 8: Evaluation results on the ”Needle In A Haystack” (NIAH) tests. DeepSeek-V3 performs well across all context window lengths up to 128K.
4.3 Long Context Extension We adopt a similar approach to DeepSeek-V2 ( DeepSeek-AI, 2024c ) to enable long context capabilities in DeepSeek-V3. After the pre-training stage, we ap
ply YaRN ( Peng et al., 2023a ) for context extension and perform two additional training phases, each comprising 1000 steps, to progressively expand the context window from 4K to
32K and then to 128K. The YaRN configuration is consistent with that used in DeepSeek-V2, being applied exclusively to the decoupled shared key . The hyper-parameters remain identi
cal across both phases, with the scale , , , and the scaling factor . In the first phase, the sequence length is set to 32K, and the batch size is 1920. During the second phase, th
e sequence length is increased to 128K, and the batch size is reduced to 480. The learning rate for both phases is set to , matching the final learning rate

142: lowing and user-preference benchmarks, with AlpacaEval 2.0 improving by 25% and ArenaHard by 17%. In addition, we compare DeepSeek-R1 with other models in Supplementary D.2 . Model
143:  safety evaluations are provided in Supplementary D.3 . A comprehensive analysis is provided in Supplementary E , including a comparison with DeepSeek-V3, performance evaluations o
144: n both fresh test sets, a breakdown of mathematical capabilities by category, and an investigation of test-time scaling behavior. Supplementary F shows that the strong reasoning ca
145: pability can be transferred to smaller models. 5 Ethics and Safety Statement With the advancement in the reasoning capabilities of DeepSeek-R1, we deeply recognize the potential et
146: hical risks. For example, R1 can be subject to jailbreak attacks, leading to the generation of dangerous content such as explosive manufacturing plans, while the enhanced reasoning
147:  capabilities enable the model to provide plans with better operational feasibility and executability. Besides, a public model is also vulnerable to further fine-tuning that could 
148: compromise inherent safety protections. In Supplementary D.3 , we present a comprehensive safety report from multiple perspectives, including performance on open-source and in-hous
149: e safety evaluation benchmarks, and safety levels across multiple languages and against jailbreak attacks. These comprehensive safety analyses conclude that the inherent safety lev
150: el of the DeepSeek-R1 model, compared to other state-of-the-art models, is generally at a moderate level (comparable to GPT-4o (2024-05-13)). Besides, when coupled with the risk co
151: ntrol system, the model’s safety level is elevated to a superior standard. 6 Conclusion, Limitation, and Future Work We present DeepSeek-R1-Zero and DeepSeek-R1, which rely on larg
152: e-scale RL to incentivize model reasoning behaviors. Our results demonstrate that pre-trained checkpoints inherently possess substantial potential for complex reasoning tasks. We b
153: elieve that the key to unlocking this potential lies not in large-scale human annotation but in the provision of hard reasoning questions, a reliable verifier, and sufficient compu
154: tational resources for reinforcement learning. Sophisticated reasoning behaviors, such as self-verification and reflection, appeared to emerge organically during the reinforcement 
155: learning process. Even if DeepSeek-R1 achieves frontier results on reasoning benchmarks, it still faces several capability limitations, as outlined below: Structure Output and Tool
156:  Use: Currently, the structural output capabilities of DeepSeek-R1 remain suboptimal compared to existing models. Moreover, DeepSeek-R1 cannot leverage tools, such as search engine
157: s and calculators, to improve the performance of output. However, as it is not hard to build an RL environment for structure output and tool use, we believe the issue will be addre
158: ssed in the next version. Token efficiency: Unlike conventional test-time computation scaling approaches, such as majority voting or Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS), DeepSeek-R1 dyn
159: amically allocates computational resources during inference according to the complexity of the problem at hand. Specifically, it uses fewer tokens to solve simple tasks, while gene
160: rating more tokens for complex tasks. Nevertheless, there remains room for further optimization in terms of token efficiency, as instances of excessive reasoning—manifested as over
161: thinking—are still observed in response to simpler questions. Language Mixing: DeepSeek-R1 is currently optimized for Chinese and English, which may result in language mixing issue
162: s when handling queries in other languages. For instance, DeepSeek-R1 might use English for reasoning and responses, even if the query is in a language other than English or Chines
163: e. We aim to address this limitation in future updates. The limitation may be related to the base checkpoint, DeepSeek-V3-Base, mainly utilizes Chinese and English, so that it can 
164: achieve better results with the two languages in reasoning. Prompting Engineering: When evaluating DeepSeek-R1, we observe that it is sensitive to prompts. Few-shot prompting consi
165: stently degrades its performance. Therefore, we recommend users directly describe the problem and specify the output format using a zero-shot setting for optimal results. Software 
166: Engineering Tasks: Due to the long evaluation times, which impact the efficiency of the RL process, large-scale RL has not been applied extensively in software engineering tasks. A
167: s a result, DeepSeek-R1 has not demonstrated a huge improvement over DeepSeek-V3 on software engineering benchmarks. Future versions will address this by implementing rejection sam
168: pling on software engineering data or incorporating asynchronous evaluations during the RL process to improve efficiency. Beyond specific capability limitations, the pure RL method
169: ology itself also presents inherent challenges: Reward Hacking: The success of pure RL depends on reliable reward signals. In this study, we ensure reward reliability through a rea
170: soning-domain rule-based reward model (RM). However, such dependable RMs are difficult to construct for certain tasks, such as writing. If the reward signal is assigned by a model 
171: instead of predefined rules, it becomes more susceptible to exploitation as training progresses, which means the policy model may find shortcuts to hack the reward model. Consequen
172: tly, for complex tasks that cannot be effectively evaluated by a reliable reward model, scaling up pure RL methods remains an open challenge. In this work, for tasks that cannot ob
173: tain a reliable signal, DeepSeek-R1 uses human annotation to create supervised data, and only conduct RL for hundreds of steps. We hope in the future, a robust reward model can be 
174: obtained to address such issues. With the advent of pure RL methods like DeepSeek-R1, the future holds immense potential for solving any task that can be effectively evaluated by a
175:  verifier, regardless of its complexity for humans. Machines equipped with such advanced RL techniques are poised to surpass human capabilities in these domains, driven by their ab
176: ility to optimize performance iteratively through trial and error. However, challenges remain for tasks where constructing a reliable reward model is inherently difficult. In such 
177: cases, the lack of a robust feedback mechanism may hinder progress, suggesting that future research should focus on developing innovative approaches to define and refine reward str
178: uctures for these complex, less verifiable problems. Furthermore, leveraging tools during the reasoning process holds significant promise. Whether it’s utilizing tools like compile
179: rs or search engines to retrieve or compute necessary information, or employing external tools—such as biological or chemical reagents, to validate final results in the real world,
180:  this integration of tool-augmented reasoning could dramatically enhance the scope and accuracy of machine-driven solutions. 7 Author List The list of authors is organized by contr

ntrol system, the model’s safety level is elevated to a superior standard. 6 Conclusion, Limitation, and Future Work We present DeepSeek-R1-Zero and DeepSeek-R1, which rely on larg

ology itself also presents inherent challenges: Reward Hacking: The success of pure RL depends on reliable reward signals. In this study, we ensure reward reliability through a rea

lines.text: \reportnumber 001 DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning DeepSeek-AI research@deepseek.com Abstract General reasoning represents a long-
standing and formidable challenge in artificial intelligence. Recent breakthroughs, exemplified by large language models (LLMs) ( Brown et al., 2020 ; OpenAI, 2023 ) and chain-of-t
hought prompting ( Wei et al., 2022b ) , have achieved considerable success on foundational reasoning tasks. However, this success is heavily contingent upon extensive human-annota
ted demonstrations, and models’ capabilities are still insufficient for more complex problems. Here we show that the reasoning abilities of LLMs can be incentivized through pure re
inforcement learning (RL), obviating the need for human-labeled reasoning trajectories. The proposed RL framework facilitates the emergent development of advanced reasoning pattern
s, such as self-reflection, verification, and dynamic strategy adaptation. Consequently, the trained model achieves superior performance on verifiable tasks such as mathematics, co
ding competitions, and STEM fields, surpassing its counterparts trained via conventional supervised learning on human demonstrations. Moreover, the emergent reasoning patterns exhi
bited by these large-scale models can be systematically harnessed to guide and enhance the reasoning capabilities of smaller models. keywords Large Language Model, Reasoning, Reinf
orcement Learning 1 Introduction Reasoning capability, the cornerstone of human intelligence, enables complex cognitive tasks ranging from mathematical problem-solving to logical d
eduction and programming. Recent advances in artificial intelligence have demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can exhibit emergent behaviors, including reasoning abiliti
es, when scaled to a sufficient size ( Wei et al., 2022a ; Kaplan et al., 2020 ) . However, achieving such capabilities in pre-training typically demands substantial computational
resources. In parallel, a complementary line of research has demonstrated that large language models can be effectively augmented through chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting. This tec
hnique, which involves either providing carefully designed few-shot examples or using minimalistic prompts such as “Let’s think step by step” ( Wei et al., 2022b ; Kojima et al., 2
022 ) , enables models to produce intermediate reasoning steps, thereby substantially enhancing their performance on complex tasks. Similarly, further performance gains have been o
bserved when models learn high-quality, multi-step reasoning trajectories during the post-training phase ( OpenAI, 2023 ; Chung et al., 2024 ) . Despite their effectiveness, these
approaches exhibit notable limitations. Their dependence on human-annotated reasoning traces hinders scalability and introduces cognitive biases. Furthermore, by constraining model
s to replicate human thought processes, their performance is inherently capped by the human-provided exemplars, which prevents the exploration of superior, non-human-like reasoning
pathways. To tackle these issues, we aim to explore the potential of LLMs for developing reasoning abilities through self-evolution in an RL framework, with minimal reliance on hu
man labeling efforts. Specifically, we build upon DeepSeek-V3-Base ( DeepSeek-AI, 2024b ) and employ Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) ( Shao et al., 2024 ) as our RL frame
work. The reward signal is solely based on the correctness of final predictions against ground-truth answers, without imposing constraints on the reasoning process itself. Notably,
we bypass the conventional supervised fine-tuning (SFT) phase before RL training. This design choice stems from our hypothesis that human-defined reasoning patterns may limit mode
l exploration, whereas unrestricted RL training can better incentivize the emergence of novel reasoning capabilities in LLMs. Through this process, detailed in Section 2 , our mode
l (referred to as DeepSeek-R1-Zero) naturally developed diverse and sophisticated reasoning behaviors. In solving reasoning problems, the model exhibits a tendency to generate long
er responses, incorporating verification, reflection, and the exploration of alternative approaches within each response. Although we do not explicitly teach the model how to reaso
n, it successfully learns improved reasoning strategies through reinforcement learning. Although DeepSeek-R1-Zero demonstrates excellent reasoning capabilities, it faces challenges
such as poor readability and language mixing, occasionally combining English and Chinese within a single chain-of-thought response. Furthermore, the rule-based RL training stage o
f DeepSeek-R1-Zero is narrowly focused on reasoning tasks, resulting in limited performance in broader areas such as writing and open-domain question answering. To address these ch
allenges, we introduce DeepSeek-R1, a model trained through a multi-stage learning framework that integrates rejection sampling, reinforcement learning, and supervised fine-tuning,
detailed in Section 3 . This training pipeline enables DeepSeek-R1 to inherit the reasoning capabilities of its predecessor, DeepSeek-R1-Zero, while aligning model behavior with h
uman preferences through additional non-reasoning data. To enable broader access to powerful AI at a lower energy cost, we have distilled several smaller models and made them publi
cly available. These distilled models exhibit strong reasoning capabilities, surpassing the performance of their original instruction-tuned counterparts. We believe that these inst
ruction-tuned versions will also significantly contribute to the research community by providing a valuable resource for understanding the mechanisms underlying long chain-of-thoug
ht (CoT) reasoning models and for fostering the development of more powerful reasoning models. We release DeepSeek-R1 series models to the public at https://huggingface.co/deepseek
-ai . 2 DeepSeek-R1-Zero We begin by elaborating on the training of DeepSeek-R1-Zero, which relies exclusively on reinforcement learning without supervised fine-tuning. To facilita
te large-scale RL efficiency, we adopt Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) ( Shao et al., 2024 ) . 2.1 Group Relative Policy Optimization GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) is the re
inforcement learning algorithm that we adopt to train DeepSeek-R1-Zero and DeepSeek-R1. It was originally proposed to simplify the training process and reduce the resource consumpt
ion of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) ( Schulman et al., 2017 ) , which is widely used in the RL stage of LLMs ( Ouyang et al., 2022 ) . For each question , GRPO samples a grou

32,768 tokens before the 8.2k step and 65,536 tokens afterward. As a result, both the performance and response length of DeepSeek-R1-Zero exhibit a significant jump at the 8.2k st

ning, generating hundreds to thousands of tokens to explore and improve its problem-solving strategies. The increase in thinking time fosters the autonomous development of sophisti

## 300 字中文综述：共同问题与研究空白
四篇均属前沿大模型的技术报告或系统卡，共同问题有三。其一，评价依赖内部基准与私有数据，能力对比缺少可复现、可第三方核验的公开流程，基准饱和与数据污染难以排除。其二，安全与对齐评估仍处起步阶段，且以中英文与文本—图像为主，对多语言、语音韵律、真实场景鲁棒性及拟人化依赖等长尾风险覆盖不足。其三，透明度有限，语料构成、清洗规则与失败案例披露不充分，系统卡与技术报告缺乏统一报告规范。
研究空白在于：缺少跨模态、跨语言、抗污染的统一评测基准与公开可复现的安全评估协议；长视频、文档细粒度感知与 GUI 智能体的真实基准仍稀缺；推理模型在无可靠验证器任务上的奖励设计与反奖励黑客机制尚待突破；token 效率、过度思考、工具调用与软件工程能力也是共性短板。未来需在可复现评测、透明数据治理与可靠奖励建模三方面协同推进，方能把"更强"转化为"可信、可用"。

## 三、500 字中文综述：共同问题与研究空白

十篇文献去重后实为四篇——GPT-4o 系统卡、Qwen2.5-VL、DeepSeek-V3 与 DeepSeek-R1；p1/p5/p9、p2/p6/p10、p3/p7、p4/p8 逐字节相同，且各文件被统一截断在约 60 KB（DeepSeek-V3 尤缺第 5–6 节）。这一事实本身即构成第一个共同问题：语料治理与可复现性不足。文件重复、版本标注混乱、正文截断，使"十篇"的独立样本量被虚增，任何按篇数计的分析都会失真，提示在文献管理与证据核查层面亟需去重、版本对齐与完整留存。

就内容而言，四篇分属"系统卡—多模态"与"高效预训练—强化学习推理"两条主线，共同问题有三。其一，评测高度依赖内部基准、私有数据与自建流程，第三方难以复现，基准饱和与数据污染难以排除，跨模型比较多在同一报告内自证。其二，安全与对齐评估尚处起步：覆盖以中英文、文本—图像为主，对语音韵律、多语言、真实场景鲁棒性及拟人化依赖等长尾风险明显不足，且多依赖模型自动打分，缺少人工与外部审计。其三，透明度有限，语料构成、清洗规则、失败案例与算力成本的完整披露不统一，系统卡与技术报告缺乏可比的报告规范。

研究空白因此清晰：亟需跨模态、跨语言、抗污染的统一公开评测与可复现的安全评估协议；长视频、文档细粒度感知与 GUI 智能体的真实基准仍稀缺；纯强化学习在无可靠验证器任务上的奖励设计与反奖励黑客机制尚未突破；token 效率、过度思考、工具调用与软件工程能力是共性短板。此外，多模态感知与长链推理的融合、以及训练/推理成本的可持续性，仍缺系统研究。唯有在可复现评测、透明数据治理与可靠奖励建模三方面协同推进，"更强"才能转化为"可信、可用"。
"}

| **D**（p4=p8） | DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning（DeepSeek-AI, 2025） | 能否不依赖人工标注的推理轨迹，仅用纯强化学习激励大模型自发涌现推理能力（自我反思、验证、策略调整）？ | 以 DeepSeek-V3-Base 为基座、GRPO 为 RL 框架；R1-Zero 跳过 SFT 直接用规则奖励（准确率+格式）做纯 RL；R1 采用多阶段管线：冷启动 SFT→推理 RL→拒绝采样+SFT（含非推理数据）→二次 RL（加入有用性/无害性奖励模型）；将推理能力蒸馏到小模型。 | 数学/代码/逻辑等可验证任务的规则奖励；约数千条冷启动数据；66000 条有用性偏好对、106000 条安全标注 prompt；评测覆盖 MMLU、MMLU-Pro、GPQA、SimpleQA、LiveCodeBench、Codeforces、AIME 2024、MATH-500、CNMO 2024、C-Eval 等。 | R1-Zero 在 AIME 2024 上 pass@1 从 15.6% 升至 77.9%（cons@16 达 86.7%），训练中出现"aha moment"，自发延长思考并涌现反思与验证；R1 在推理基准达前沿水平（AIME 79.8、MATH-500 97.3、Codeforces 百分位 96.3、LiveCodeBench 65.9），通用指令遵循大幅提升（AlpacaEval2.0 +25%、ArenaHard +17%）；蒸馏小模型推理能力优于原指令模型。 | 明确列出：结构化输出与工具使用能力偏弱；token 效率不足、简单题存在过度思考；语言混合（主要优化中英文，其他语言可能混用英语推理）；对提示敏感、few-shot 反而降分；软件工程任务提升有限；纯 RL 依赖可靠奖励，写作等不可验证任务易奖励黑客，可靠奖励建模仍是开放难题；安全水平总体中等，可被越狱/微调破坏。 |

## 三、500 字中文综述：共同问题与研究空白

十篇文献去重后实为四篇——GPT-4o 系统卡、Qwen2.5-VL、DeepSeek-V3 与 DeepSeek-R1；p1/p5/p9、p2/p6/p10、p3/p7、p4/p8 逐字节相同，且各文件被统一截断在约 60 KB（DeepSeek-V3 尤缺第 5–6 节）。这一事实本身即构成第一个共同问题：语料治理与可复现性不足。文件重复、版本标注混乱、正文截断，使"十篇"的独立样本量被虚增，任何按篇数计的分析都会失真，提示在文献管理与证据核查层面亟需去重、版本对齐与完整留存。

就内容而言，四篇分属"系统卡—多模态"与"高效预训练—强化学习推理"两条主线，共同问题有三。其一，评测高度依赖内部基准、私有数据与自建流程，第三方难以复现，基准饱和与数据污染难以排除，跨模型比较多在同一报告内自证。其二，安全与对齐评估尚处起步：覆盖以中英文、文本—图像为主，对语音韵律、多语言、真实场景鲁棒性及拟人化依赖等长尾风险明显不足，且多依赖模型自动打分，缺少人工与外部审计。其三，透明度有限，语料构成、清洗规则、失败案例与算力成本的完整披露不统一，系统卡与技术报告缺乏可比的报告规范。

研究空白因此清晰：亟需跨模态、跨语言、抗污染的统一公开评测与可复现的安全评估协议；长视频、文档细粒度感知与 GUI 智能体的真实基准仍稀缺；纯强化学习在无可靠验证器任务上的奖励设计与反奖励黑客机制尚未突破；token 效率、过度思考、工具调用与软件工程能力是共性短板。此外，多模态感知与长链推理的融合、以及训练/推理成本的可持续性，仍缺系统研究。唯有在可复现评测、透明数据治理与可靠奖励建模三方面协同推进，"更强"才能转化为"可信、可用"。

38: 
39: 就内容而言，四篇分属"系统卡—多模态"与"高效预训练—强化学习推理"两条主线，共同问题有三。其一，评测高度依赖内部基准、私有数据与自建流程，第三方难以复现，基准饱和与数据污染难以排除，跨模型比较多在同一报告内自证。其二，安全与对齐评估尚处起步：覆盖以中英文、文本—图像为主，对语音韵律、多语言、真实场景鲁棒性及拟人化依赖等长尾风险明显不足，且多依赖模型自动打分，缺少人工与外部审计。其三，透明度有限，语料构成、清洗规则、失败案例与算力成本的完整披露不统一，系统卡与技术报告缺乏可比的报告规范。
40: 
41: 研究空白因此清晰：亟需跨模态、跨语言、抗污染的统一公开评测与可复现的安全评估协议；长视频、文档细粒度感知与 GUI 智能体的真实基准仍稀缺；纯强化学习在无可靠验证器任务上的奖励设计与反奖励黑客机制尚未突破；token 效率、过度思考、工具调用与软件工程能力是共性短板。此外，多模态感知与长链推理的融合、以及训练/推理成本的可持续性，仍缺系统研究。唯有在可复现评测、透明数据治理与可靠奖励建模三方面协同推进，"更强"才能转化为"可信、可用"。

## 四、共同模式：哪些局限是跨论文复现的

把四篇并置可见，局限并非各自孤立，而是反复出现几类结构性共同模式：

1. **评测效度与可复现性模式。** 四篇都依赖内部基准、私有/合成数据与自建流程：GPT-4o 用 TTS 代理语音评测，Qwen 与 DeepSeek 用自建/合成数据与内部评测。共同后果是代理失真、基准饱和与数据污染难以排除、第三方难以复现，且跨模型比较多在各自报告内自证。
2. **覆盖偏置模式。** 语言与场景普遍以中英文、文本/图像为主，对多语言、语音韵律、真实长尾与低资源场景覆盖不足（GPT-4o 非英语过度拒答、Qwen 中英文偏置、R1 语言混合），是四篇共有的分布性盲区。
3. **"评估先行、机制滞后"的安全对齐模式。** 安全水平多为中等、可被越狱或微调破坏；拟人化、版权、情感依赖等长尾社会风险多为定性讨论，缺少长期、多样化人群的实证，安全评估跑在机制与治理之前。
4. **工程与成本依赖模式。** 强性能都建立在专用集群、大规模算力与复杂系统工程之上（GPT-4o 的 TTS/红队管线、Qwen 的 4.1T 语料训练、V3 的 MoE/FP8、R1 的大规模 RL），可移植性、成本可持续性与复现门槛构成共同约束。
5. **透明度模式。** 语料构成、清洗规则、失败案例与成本披露口径不统一，系统卡与技术报告缺乏可比的报告规范，使外部审计困难。

值得补充的是：本次语料"十篇实为四篇、且被统一截断"的重复与残缺，正是上述"可复现性/透明度"问题在文献管理层面的镜像——它提醒读者，除了模型本身的局限，证据链的组织方式同样会影响结论的可靠性。

DeepSeek-R1——能力短板、奖励依赖与安全可被削弱。** 其局限在文中列得最明确。能力层面：结构化输出与工具调用偏弱（不能用搜索、计算器等外部工具）；token 效率不足，简单题存在过度思考；存在语言混合，主要优化中英文、其他语言可能用英语推理；对提示敏感，few-shot 反而降分；软件工程任务因评测耗时、RL 难以大规模展开而提升有限。方法层面更根本：纯 RL 高度依赖可靠奖励，其成功建立在数学、代码等可规则验证的任务上；对写作等不可验证任务，模型奖励易被"奖励黑客"利用，如何为复杂任务构建稳健奖励模型仍是开放难题，这也是纯 RL 难以推广的根本瓶颈。安全层面：总体安全为中等（约与 GPT-4o 相当），可被越狱攻击，也可被进一步微调破坏原有安全对齐。概括为"能力短板 + 奖励依赖 + 安全可被削弱"。

## 四、共同模式：哪些局限是跨论文复现的

把四篇并置可见，局限并非各自孤立，而是反复出现几类结构性共同模式：

1. **评测效度与可复现性模式。** 四篇都依赖内部基准、私有/合成数据与自建流程：GPT-4o 用 TTS 代理语音评测，Qwen 与 DeepSeek 用自建/合成数据与内部评测。共同后果是代理失真、基准饱和与数据污染难以排除、第三方难以复现，且跨模型比较多在各自报告内自证。
2. **覆盖偏置模式。** 语言与场景普遍以中英文、文本/图像为主，对多语言、语音韵律、真实长尾与低资源场景覆盖不足（GPT-4o 非英语过度拒答、Qwen 中英文偏置、R1 语言混合），是四篇共有的分布性盲区。
3. **"评估先行、机制滞后"的安全对齐模式。** 安全水平多为中等、可被越狱或微调破坏；拟人化、版权、情感依赖等长尾社会风险多为定性讨论，缺少长期、多样化人群的实证，安全评估跑在机制与治理之前。
4. **工程与成本依赖模式。** 强性能都建立在专用集群、大规模算力与复杂系统工程之上（GPT-4o 的 TTS/红队管线、Qwen 的 4.1T 语料训练、V3 的 MoE/FP8、R1 的大规模 RL），可移植性、成本可持续性与复现门槛构成共同约束。
5. **透明度模式。** 语料构成、清洗规则、失败案例与成本披露口径不统一，系统卡与技术报告缺乏可比的报告规范，使外部审计困难。

值得补充的是：本次语料"十篇实为四篇、且被统一截断"的重复与残缺，正是上述"可复现性/透明度"问题在文献管理层面的镜像——它提醒读者，除了模型本身的局限，证据链的组织方式同样会影响结论的可靠性。

## 五、500 字中文综述：共同问题与研究空白

十篇文献去重后实为四篇——GPT-4o 系统卡、Qwen2.5-VL、DeepSeek-V3 与 DeepSeek-R1；p1/p5/p9、p2/p6/p10、p3/p7、p4/p8 逐字节相同，且各文件被统一截断在约 60 KB（DeepSeek-V3 尤缺第 5–6 节）。这一事实本身即构成第一个共同问题：语料治理与可复现性不足。文件重复、版本标注混乱、正文截断，使"十篇"的独立样本量被虚增，任何按篇数计的分析都会失真，提示在文献管理与证据核查层面亟需去重、版本对齐与完整留存。

就内容而言，四篇分属"系统卡—多模态"与"高效预训练—强化学习推理"两条主线，共同问题有三。其一，评测高度依赖内部基准、私有数据与自建流程，第三方难以复现，基准饱和与数据污染难以排除，跨模型比较多在同一报告内自证。其二，安全与对齐评估尚处起步：覆盖以中英文、文本—图像为主，对语音韵律、多语言、真实场景鲁棒性及拟人化依赖等长尾风险明显不足，且多依赖模型自动打分，缺少人工与外部审计。其三，透明度有限，语料构成、清洗规则、失败案例与算力成本的完整披露不统一，系统卡与技术报告缺乏可比的报告规范。

## 三、各篇局限详述（逐篇展开）

**A. GPT-4o System Card——评测代理失真、真实鲁棒性与长尾风险未量化。** 其局限首先出在评测工具上：语音能力主要借 TTS 把文本基准转成音频来测，而这一转换对公式、代码、依赖空白与符号排版的输入天然不适用，合成语音也无法代表真实对话中的韵律、情绪、背景噪声与串话，故测得的"能力"与"安全"都可能偏离真实使用分布，作者亦承认错误可能来自 TTS 而非模型。其次是鲁棒性缺口：低质量音频、回声、音频扰动以及生成过程中的打断都会削弱安全表现，模型仍可被诱导复述虚假信息与阴谋论。第三是公平与语言覆盖：非英语场景存在过度拒答，输出可能带非母语口音，五种非洲语言虽缩小了与英语的差距但差距仍在。第四是长尾风险刻画不足：版权、拟人化与情感依赖等社会影响多为定性讨论，缺乏长期、多样化人群的实证；医学评测只测静态知识、不测真实临床工作流，且多项基准趋于饱和、区分度下降。概括为"评测代理失真 + 真实场景鲁棒性不足 + 长尾社会风险未量化"。

**B. Qwen2.5-VL——多模态对齐、数据/语言偏置与真实基准缺位。** 报告未设独立局限章节，短板需从方法与实验反推。首先，多模态对齐仍是核心难题：作者明确指出中间推理步骤可能忽略或误读视觉线索，CoT 在跨模态任务上的可靠验证尚不成熟。其次，数据与语言偏置明显：SFT 数据以中英文为主，多语言 OCR 虽扩展语种但整体覆盖有限；训练大量依赖合成与自建数据（约 100 万合成图表、600 万表格），存在合成分布偏差与真实长尾场景泛化不足的风险。第三，评测以英文基准为主，MMMU、DocVQA、OCRBench 等虽亮眼，但对真实业务文档、噪声图像、低资源语言与对抗样本的鲁棒性验证不足，难以排除基准与训练数据重叠（污染）带来的高估。第四，效率与成本：72B 模型训练与推理开销大，窗口注意力虽降低视觉端计算，但长视频（数百帧、逾 2 万 token）仍受上下文与算力约束。概括为"对齐可靠性 + 数据/语言偏置 + 真实基准缺位 + 成本约束"。

**C. DeepSeek-V3——能力偏科、系统工程脆弱与复现门槛高。** 该文本为节选（缺第 5–6 节），完整局限未系统给出，需结合摘要与可见结果审慎归纳。其一，能力上仍有明确差距：英语事实知识（SimpleQA）落后 GPT-4o 与 Claude，工程类/软件任务略低于 Claude-3.5，说明优势集中于数学、代码与中文事实性，通用知识与复杂工程仍是短板。其二，效率优势伴随工程脆弱性：MoE 路由、FP8 混合精度与跨节点 all-to-all 通信都是强耦合的系统工程，依赖专用 H800 集群与大量前期架构/数据研究（论文强调 557.6 万美元仅含"官方训练"，不含前期试错成本），可移植性与复现门槛高。其三，训练稳定性结论基于单次大规模运行，"无 loss spike、无回滚"的可推广性仍需更多独立复现验证。其四，数据侧对合成数据与污染的影响缺少量化评估，14.8T 语料的构成与清洗透明度有限。概括为"能力偏科 + 系统工程脆弱 + 复现门槛高 + 数据治理不透明"。

**D. DeepSeek-R1——能力短板、奖励依赖与安全可被削弱。** 其局限在文中列得最明确。能力层面：结构化输出与工具调用偏弱（不能用搜索、计算器等外部工具）；token 效率不足，简单题存在过度思考；存在语言混合，主要优化中英文、其他语言可能用英语推理；对提示敏感，few-shot 反而降分；软件工程任务因评测耗时、RL 难以大规模展开而提升有限。方法层面更根本：纯 RL 高度依赖可靠奖励，其成功建立在数学、代码等可规则验证的任务上；对写作等不可验证任务，模型奖励易被"奖励黑客"利用，如何为复杂任务构建稳健奖励模型仍是开放难题，这也是纯 RL 难以推广的根本瓶颈。安全层面：总体安全为中等（约与 GPT-4o 相当），可被越狱攻击，也可被进一步微调破坏原有安全对齐。概括为"能力短板 + 奖励依赖 + 安全可被削弱"。
## 四、共同模式：哪些局限是跨论文复现的
把四篇并置可见，局限并非各自孤立，而是反复出现几类结构性共同模式：
1. **评测效度与可复现性模式。** 四篇都依赖内部基准、私有/合成数据与自建流程：GPT-4o 用 TTS 代理语音评测，Qwen 与 DeepSeek 用自建/合成数据与内部评测。共同后果是代理失真、基准饱和与数据污染难以排除、第三方难以复现，且跨模型比较多在各自报告内自证。
2. **覆盖偏置模式。** 语言与场景普遍以中英文、文本/图像为主，对多语言、语音韵律、真实长尾与低资源场景覆盖不足（GPT-4o 非英语过度拒答、Qwen 中英文偏置、R1 语言混合），是四篇共有的分布性盲区。
3. **"评估先行、机制滞后"的安全对齐模式。** 安全水平多为中等、可被越狱或微调破坏；拟人化、版权、情感依赖等长尾社会风险多为定性讨论，缺少长期、多样化人群的实证，安全评估跑在机制与治理之前。
4. **工程与成本依赖模式。** 强性能都建立在专用集群、大规模算力与复杂系统工程之上（GPT-4o 的 TTS/红队管线、Qwen 的 4.1T 语料训练、V3 的 MoE/FP8、R1 的大规模 RL），可移植性、成本可持续性与复现门槛构成共同约束。
5. **透明度模式。** 语料构成、清洗规则、失败案例与成本披露口径不统一，系统卡与技术报告缺乏可比的报告规范，使外部审计困难。
值得补充的是：本次语料"十篇实为四篇、且被统一截断"的重复与残缺，正是上述"可复现性/透明度"问题在文献管理层面的镜像——它提醒读者，除了模型本身的局限，证据链的组织方式同样会影响结论的可靠性。

**一、引言：研究背景、范围与文献构成**
- 拟引用：A、B、C、D
- 要点：以大模型"更强→更可信可用"为线索，界定综述范围；交代语料去重后实为四篇（A/B/C/D），按"多模态—高效训练—强化学习推理"两条主线组织；提出贯穿全文的问题框架（能力、效率、可信性三者张力）；预告共同问题与研究空白。

**二、多模态与 omni 模型：架构、感知与智能体能力**
- 拟引用：A、B（可对照 C 的纯文本基座）
- 要点：端到端 omni 架构（文本/音频/图像/视频统一网络，A）；原生动态分辨率 ViT + 窗口注意力、2D-RoPE/3D patch（B）；绝对时间对齐的 MRoPE 与动态 FPS 处理长视频（B）；统一 omni-document 解析与 GUI/移动端智能体（B）；多模态/跨语言能力评测表现与语音交互延迟（A、B）。

**三、高效训练与推理：MoE、低精度与系统工程**
- 拟引用：C、B
- 要点：MLA 低秩 KV 压缩与 DeepSeekMoE（671B 总参/37B 激活，C）；无辅助损失负载均衡 + 序列级互补平衡损失、多 token 预测目标（C）；FP8 混合精度、DualPipe 流水线与跨节点 all-to-all 优化、两阶段长上下文扩展（C）；视觉端窗口注意力/特征压缩带来的效率收益（B）；"性能—成本"权衡与 2.788M GPU 小时/$5.576M 的训练经济性（C）。

**四、推理能力的激励与对齐：强化学习与蒸馏**
- 拟引用：D、C
- 要点：纯 RL + GRPO、R1-Zero 跳过 SFT 的可行性（D）；规则奖励（准确率+格式）与"aha moment"、自我反思/验证的涌现（D）；多阶段 R1 管线（冷启动 SFT→推理 RL→拒绝采样+SFT→二次 RL）与蒸馏到小模型（D）；从 R1 蒸馏推理能力改进入 V3 的后训练（C）；纯 RL 的边界——可靠奖励缺失任务（写作等）的奖励黑客问题（D）。

**五、安全、评测与可信性：共同局限与研究空白**
- 拟引用：A、B、C、D
- 要点：评测效度与可复现性——内部/私有/合成数据、TTS 代理失真、基准饱和与数据污染（A、B、C）；覆盖偏置——中英文、文本/图像为主，多语言、语音韵律、长尾与低资源不足（A、B、D）；安全"评估先行、机制滞后"——安全多为中等、可被越狱/微调破坏，拟人化/版权/情感依赖仅定性（A、D）；工程与成本依赖、透明度不足（C、D）；凝练研究空白：跨模态抗污染统一评测与可复现安全评估协议、长视频/文档/GUI 真实基准、无可靠验证器任务的可靠奖励建模、token 效率与成本可持续性。

---

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

The top layer of this framework is multi-modal reasoning, which is enhanced by leveraging the latest Qwen2.5 LLM and employing multi-modal QA data construction. A spectrum of works have promoted the development of multimodal large models, characterized by architectural design, visual input processing, and data curation. One of the primary drivers of progress in LVLMs is the continuous innovation in architecture. The studies presented in ( Alayrac et al., 2022 ; Li et al., 2022a ; Li et al., 2023b ; Liu et al., 2023b ; Liu et al., 2023a ; Wang et al., 2024i ; Zhang et al., 2024b ; Wang et al., 2023 ) have incrementally shaped the current paradigm, which typically consists of a visual encoder, a cross-modal projector, and LLM. Fine-grained perception models have emerged as another crucial area. Models like ( Xiao et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2023c ; Ren et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2024a ; Zhang et al., 2024d ; Peng et al., 2023 ; Deitke et al., 2024 ) have pushed the boundaries of what is possible in terms of detailed visual understanding. The architectures of Omni ( Li et al., 2024g ; Li et al., 2025b ; Ye et al., 2024 ) and MoE ( Riquelme et al., 2021 ; Lee et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2024h ; Li et al., 2024c ; Wu et al., 2024b ) also inspire the future evolution of LVLMs. Enhancements in visual encoders ( Chen et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2024b ; Liang et al., 2025 ) and resolution scaling ( Li et al., 2023c ; Ye et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2023a ) have played a pivotal role in improving the quality of practical visual understanding. Curating data with more diverse scenarios and higher-quality is an essential step in training advanced LVLMs. The efforts proposed in ( Guo et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2024d ; Liu et al., 2024a ; Chen e

t al., 2024a ; Tong et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2024a ) are highly valuable contributions to this endeavor. However, despite their remarkable progress, vision-language models currently face developmental bottlenecks, including computational complexity, limited contextual understanding, poor fine-grained visual perception, and inconsistent performance across varied sequence length. In this report, we introduce the latest work Qwen2.5-VL, which continues the open-source philosophy of the Qwen series, achieving and even surpassing top-tier closed-source models on various benchmarks. Technically, our contributions are four-folds: (1) We implement window attention in the visual encoder to optimize inference efficiency; (2) We introduce dynamic FPS sampling, extending dynamic resolution to the temporal dimension and enabling comprehensive video understanding across varied sampling rates; (3) We upgrade MRoPE in the temporal domain by aligning to absolute time, thereby facilitating more sophisticated temporal sequence learning; (4) We make significant efforts in curating high-quality data for both pre-training and supervised fine-tuning, further scaling the pre-training corpus from 1.2 trillion tokens to 4.1 trillion tokens. The sparkling characteristics of Qwen2.5-VL are as follows: — Powerful document parsing capabilities: Qwen2.5-VL upgrades text recognition to omni-document parsing, excelling in processing multi-scene, multilingual, and various built-in (handwriting, tables, charts, chemical formulas, and music sheets) documents. — Precise object grounding across formats: Qwen2.5-VL unlocks improved accuracy in detecting, pointing, and counting objects, accommodating absolute coordinate and JSON formats for advanced spatial reasoning. — Ultra-long video understanding and fin
=== 5400 ===
e-grained video grounding: Our model extends native dynamic resolution to the temporal dimension, enhancing the ability to understand videos lasting hours while extracting event segments in seconds. — Enhanced agent Functionality for computer and mobile devices: Leverage advanced grounding, reasoning, and decision-making abilities, boosting the model with superior agent functionality on smartphones and computers. Approach In this section, we first outline the architectural updates of the Qwen2.5-VL series models and provide an overview of the data and training details. Figure 1: The Qwen2.5-VL framework demonstrates the integration of a vision encoder and a language model decoder to process multimodal inputs, including images and videos. The vision encoder is designed to handle inputs at their native resolution and supports dynamic FPS sampling. Images of varying sizes and video frames with different FPS rates are dynamically mapped to token sequences of varying lengths. Notably, MRoPE aligns time IDs with absolute time along the temporal dimension, enabling the model to better comprehend temporal dynamics, such as the pace of events and precise moment localization. The processed visual data is subsequently fed into the Qwen2.5 LM Decoder. We have re-engineered the vision transformer (ViT) architecture, incorporating advanced components such as FFN with SwiGLU activation, RMSNorm for normalization, and window-based attention mechanisms to enhance performance and efficiency. 2.1 Model Architecture The overall model architecture of Qwen2.5-VL consists of three components: Large Language Model : The Qwen2.5-VL series adopts large language models as its foundational component. The model is initialized with pre-trained weights from the Qwen2.5 LLM. To better meet the demands
=== 7200 ===
 of multimodal understanding, we have modified the 1D RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding) to our Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding Aligned to Absolute Time. Vision Encoder : The vision encoder of Qwen2.5-VL employs a redesigned Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture. Structurally, we incorporate 2D-RoPE and window attention to support native input resolutions while accelerating the computation of the entire visual encoder. During both training and inference, the height and width of the input images are resized to multiples of 28 before being fed into the ViT. The vision encoder processes images by splitting them into patches with a stride of 14, generating a set of image features. We provide a more detailed introduction to the vision encoder in Section 2.1.1 . MLP-based Vision-Language Merger : To address the efficiency challenges posed by long sequences of image features, we adopt a simple yet effective approach to compress the feature sequences before feeding them into the large language model (LLM). Specifically, instead of directly using the raw patch features extracted by the Vision Transformer (ViT), we first group spatially adjacent sets of four patch features. These grouped features are then concatenated and passed through a two-layer multi-layer perceptron (MLP) to project them into a dimension that aligns with the text embeddings used in the LLM. This method not only reduces computational costs but also provides a flexible way to dynamically compress image feature sequences of varying lengths. <skill_instructions>
# 论文降AI率 · 去AI味 · 风格自然化（paper-rewriter）

**TL;DR**：`python scripts/pipeline.py draft.txt -o out.txt` → 读报告 →（要排优先级
就 `plan.py --handoff`）→ 按 style_guide 深改 → `verify.py` → 完成；Word 直读；守卫保数字引用。
**阅读地图（30 秒路由，等价 [references/INDEX.md](references/INDEX.md)）**：上手→快速上手 · 排错→[pitfalls](references/pitfalls.md)+[errors](references/errors.md) · CI/agent→自动化节 · 边界→[honest_boundaries](references/honest_boundaries.md) · 场景→[best_practices](references/best_practices.md) · 深改流程→[deep_rewrite_guide](references/deep_rewrite_guide.md) · PDF 置信度→[pdf_confidence](references/pdf_confidence.md) · 权限质询→[permissions](references/permissions.md) · 程序化→[api](references/api.md)。
**两层分工一句话**：机械清理（transform/pipeline 自动，确定性）与质量深改（agent 按 style_guide）是两层——先跑 pipeline 看报告再决定深改。

中英双语的学术写作风格工具箱：找出书面语里生硬、模板化、机器腔的表达模式，清掉
机械垃圾，按写作质量原则深改——每一步都带完整性护栏。

> **一句话路由**：改语法、改通顺、按期刊格式润色 → 用润色工具（paper-polisher-pro）；
> 去模板腔、清模型残留、降AI率/去AI味的风格自查与改写 → 用本工具。两者都要时先润色再跑本管线。

## 学术诚信护栏——先读这一节

- **正当用途**：润色自己的稿件；在学校/期刊**允许或要求披露**的前提下，把 AI 辅助
  的文本对齐到自己的行文习惯；清理合规草稿里粘贴带进的模型残留（oaicite/[cite:]
  等垃圾 token）；提升正式文体的清晰度、节奏与具体性。
- **不做的事**：不用于误代署名、隐瞒按规定应披露的 AI 使用、对抗学术诚信审查。
  如果请求的表述是「改到没人看得出来」「帮我瞒过审查」，agent 应拒绝这一目的、
  说明披露义务，并转而提供正当的质量改写路径。运行本技能的 agent 有责任守住这条线。
- **本工具从不动数据**：数字、p 值、置信区间、DOI、PMID、年份、术语全部由
  `verify.py` 守卫（见下）。文字可以改好，事实一个不能少。
- 合规：中国 AIGC 标识办法（2025-09-01 施行）、期刊披露政策与 arXiv 政策要点
  见 `references/compliance.md`——披露义务的主体是作者，不是工具。

## 能力×边界（分工 + 做到/做不到 + 去处）

| 能力 | 做到 | 做不到（边界） | 去处 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 风格自查 | 套话密度/句长均匀/公文腔启发式报告，章节感知降权；.md 输入自动剥离结构（医学知识库友好） | 非 AI 检测器——流畅模型文本几乎不触发（低分≠无 AI 参与） | `detect.py`；边界详见 [honest_boundaries](references/honest_boundaries.md) |
| 机械清理 | 模型残留（oaicite/[cite:]）、聊天客套、标点归一、全角数字 | 不改写句式——只做零信息损失层 | `transform.py`（`--deep` 句式级） |
| 质量深改 | 去模板化/节奏/具体性/立场（指南七步） | 不编造数据；凭空新增数字被守卫告警（W_NUM_ADDED，人工核对） | **agent 本人**按 style_guide；交接块 `plan --handoff` |
| 完整性守卫 | 数字/DOI/PMID/年份/术语原样保留，篡改即 exit 1（FAIL 自带怎么修处方+原句锚点） | 真伪判断——以原始数据为准，工具只核一致性 | `verify.py` |
| 前后对比 | 特征分变化+完整性判定+画像差值 | 不替代人工通读 | `compare.py` / `stylecheck --compare` |
| 术语一致性 | 八域 27 组变体（HF/心力衰竭/心衰 一组报齐）；`--batch` 跨文件漂移（各文件各自一致、合起来不一致） | 不判断术语用得对不对，只查称谓统一 | `check_terms.py --pack` / `--batch` |
| 统计一致性 | 百分比清单求和（划分用语句）/跨文件分组 n/p 与 P 风格 | 非统计审查——不判定结果真伪 | `check_stats.py`（`--batch` 跨文件） |
| 改写动作明细 | 删八股开场（众所周知→直入论点）/拆「不仅X而且Y」/清残留/标点全角化/２０２５→2025 | ——（全部确定性零信息损失） | `transform --deep` 自动 |
| 深改动作明细 | 黑话/翻译腔替换、节奏、具体性（**绝不编造数据**） | 重写句必须过 verify 才算完成 | agent 深改 |


**功能状态（v4.2.0）**——⚠️ 行 = 实验性（可能拒收合法文件或需人工复核）；稳定能力只按代际归行，逐项明细见 references/errors.md 与各专题文档：

| 能力 | 状态 | 版本 |
|---|---|---|
| ⚠️ **PDF 直读+置信度自评**（嵌字体/ToUnicode 先试抽取封顶「中」；硬门闸校准表见 references/pdf_confidence.md；**v3.8.0 起缺省门=中**——乱码形态默认拒收，`--pdf-min-confidence 低` 恢复仅标注） | ⚠️ 实验性 | v1.6–3.8 |
| 核心五件·章节感知·句级计划（plan --handoff）·守卫自学习·机器退出码·超时/批量重试·集中异常·--deep·全角归一 | 稳定 | v1.0–2.9 |
| 风格画像·最佳实践手册·--terms auto·术语变体组（8 域 27 组）·统计一致性守卫·投稿自查包（--bundle）·HTML/--track·markdown 感知扫描 | 稳定 | v2.6–3.6 |
| 批量断点续传（--batch + --resume）·跨文件术语漂移（check_terms --batch）·报错信息人话化 | 稳定 | v3.7 |
| **PDF 缺省安全门=中+批量熔断**（同批 ≥3 个 PDF 被拒→批级警告〔不中止批处理〕，直指源头质量）·**pipeline --handoff**（一句命令产出清理+守卫+逐句深改指令单）·触发条件收拢进主文档 | 稳定 | v3.8 |
| **分块扫描降级**（单块超时→2× 预算重试→标记降级继续，报告带覆盖率注记；全块失败响亮报错；--exit-verdict 按不完整扫描拦停）·**verify 处方化输出**（每类违规附「怎么修」+数字丢失附原句锚点+修复三步；JSON 带 remedies 字段） | 稳定 | v3.9 |
| **编码自适应**（UTF-16/GBK 自动转码+标注+meta.encoding）·**批量并发隔离**（flock 锁内合并，双进程互不覆盖） | 稳定 | v4.0 |
| **pipeline --batch 降级接线**（批量内超大文件单块超时→降级继续，行内 ⚠[降级] 标记+门禁拦停——stability 系列收尾）·**深改交接块语言感知**（英文稿指令单首选锚 style_guide_en.md，中文稿 style_guide_zh.md） | 稳定 | v4.2 |

**规模上限**：单块 800,000 字符（块间 2000 重叠）· 文件 50MB · 单步 120 秒。**PDF 置信度分档**：高=放心用 · 中=抽查关键数字 · 低=乱码形态（v3.8 起缺省拒收）。

## 自动化与 CI 集成（v2.3.0）

所有判定双口径机器可读：

- **缺省口径（人读流程）**：`verify.py` 独占退出码 0/1/2（1=完整性 FAIL）；
  detect/transform/compare/pipeline 跑完恒 0，判定写在报告里。不要按它们的
  缺省退出码写分支。
- **机器口径**——detect / compare / pipeline 加 `--exit-verdict`（或等价短别名
  `--ci`，v3.1.0 起，方便 CI 里少打字）：
  `0` 干净（低档、无残留）· `3` 风格特征中及以上（需深改）· `4` 命中模型残留
  （先跑 transform）· `1` 完整性 FAIL（仅 pipeline 产出，与 verify 契约同义）·
  `2` 用法错误（不受影响）。**pipeline 是唯一 1/3/4 全档门禁**，CI 推荐：
  `pipeline.py 原稿.txt --rewrite 改稿.txt --terms terms.txt --exit-verdict`。
- **JSON**：`detect -j`（完整扫描结果）、`pipeline --json`（前后分/verify 判定/
  `exit_verdict` 字段/处置提示/深改简报）、`compare --json`（变化量+verify）、
  `plan.py --json`（句级队列+预算投影）。一行门禁示例：
  `python scripts/pipeline.py 原稿.txt --rewrite 改稿.txt --json --exit-verdict || echo "拦截: $?"`
- 两套口径的退出码全表：`references/errors.md` 第一节。

## 快速上手

**普通作者怎么开口**（不用记命令，把这些话原样说给 agent 即可）：

| 你可以这样说 | agent 会做的 |
|---|---|
| 「帮我把这篇论文的 AI 味去掉 / 降一下 AI 率」 | detect 自查 → transform 清残留 → 按指南深改 → verify 守卫 |
| 「这段读起来太模板腔了 / 太像 AI 写的」 | 同上，重点走深改（style_guide 去八股） |
| 「文里有 oaicite、[cite: 1] 这种乱码残留」 | transform 一步清掉（确定性，不碰你的句子） |
| 「先告诉我哪几句最该改」 | `plan.py` 出句级优先级清单（要交接给另一个 agent 就加 `--handoff`） |
| 「改完了，帮我确认没改坏数字和引用」 | `verify.py` 守卫 + `compare.py` 前后对比 |
| 「给我一份风格体检报告 / 量化看看改没变好」 | `stylecheck.py` 画像（单稿体检或 `--compare` 看差值） |
| 「查查数字有没有前后打架 / 百分比加起来对不对」 | `check_stats.py` 统计一致性报告（退出码同 check_terms） |
| 「给我一份能直接发给导师/编辑的自查材料」 | `pipeline.py 原稿 --bundle 目录` 生成投稿自查包（六件套） |
| 「扫到的 XX 是正常术语，别再报它」 | `learn_guards.py` 固化守卫，类似上下文下不再误报（守卫按上下文窗口豁免，全新语境仍会报） |


无需 agent——以下全部命令可直接在终端运行。
所有脚本内建 `--help`（完整参数说明）与 `--version`。常用参数语义：

| 参数 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `--profile general` | 非学术文本：降权八股/公文信号 |
| `--deep` | 确定性句式转换（句首八股删除/不仅合并） |
| `--exit-verdict` | CI/agent 门禁机器退出码（见自动化节） |
| `--structure` | 章节感知评分（IMRaD） |
| `--step-timeout 秒` | 单步墙钟预算（缺省 120） |
| `--terms 文件` | 完整性守卫术语表（extract_terms.py 生成草稿） |
| `--handoff 文件` | 一句命令随管线产出逐句深改指令单（v3.8.0） |

一条命令（自查→清理→深改简报→完整性守卫）：

```bash
python scripts/pipeline.py draft.txt -o out.txt --terms terms.txt
```

- **可视化/批量/章节**：`--html` 单文件报告（compare 含逐句对照）；`--batch 目录` 汇总；`detect --structure` 分章评分（方法/结果按领域惯例降权，各章原始分逐项展示）。
- **输入格式**：`.txt`/`.md` 直读（**UTF-8/UTF-16〔带 BOM〕/GBK 编码自动识别转码**，v4.0） · `.docx`（Word）直读 · PDF 实验性直读
  （**v3.8.0 缺省安全门=中：乱码形态直接拒收**，`低` 恢复仅标注——见 faq Q15）。
- **术语表**：`python scripts/extract_terms.py draft.txt -o terms.txt` 自动抽候选，
  人工删改后给 `--terms`；任何运行加 `--suggestions 路径.md` 同时出修订建议工作单。

非学术文本（博客、公众号、公文）加 `--profile general`，学术八股/公文过渡信号
降权 60% 减少误报；默认 `academic` 按学术论文口径标定。

或分步执行（请在技能所在目录内运行，或把 `scripts/…` 换成绝对路径）：

```bash
python scripts/detect.py draft.txt            # 风格自查（-j JSON / -s 只看分）
python scripts/transform.py draft.txt -o step1.txt
# ……按指南对 step1.txt 做质量深改……
python scripts/verify.py draft.txt step2.txt --terms terms.txt
python scripts/compare.py draft.txt step2.txt
```

端到端完整输入输出样例：`references/examples.md`。统一错误码与处置速查：
`references/errors.md`。**集中式常见错误用法清单（27 条）：`references/pitfalls.md`**
——首次实战前先读。Python API 参考：`references/api.md`。常见问题：
`references/faq.md`。

修订追踪：transform/pipeline 加 `--track base` 把机械清理的**每一处修改**记录为
base.md+base.json 可审计清单。

### Agent 调用协议

被触发时先选路径，再执行：

- **触发词**：论文降AI率 / 去AI味 / 去AI味改写 / 降AI改写 / 风格自然化 /
  写作风格自查 / 论文改写 / 学术改写 / 段落改写 / 表达优化 / 去模板腔 /
  翻译腔清理（=欧化句式：「被…所」「对…进行」「…性/…化」堆叠、长定语链——见 style_guide_zh 第 5 步）/
  论文润色（限风格自然化语义，见下方消歧） → 跑上面的管线。
  （参数速查表见「快速上手」节；两套退出码表见 references/errors.md——
  均从本节链接直达，避免跨节翻找。）
- **场景直达（v3.8.0 收拢，不再散落 references）**：CI/批量门禁 → `--exit-verdict`（短别名 `--ci`）；
  批量中断 → `--batch 目录 --resume`；误报固化 → `learn_guards.py from-text`；
  深改无从下手 → `pipeline 原稿 -o 改稿 --handoff 交接块.md` 一句出逐句指令单。
- **语义消歧（本工具 ≠ 润色工具）**：「论文改写/润色」指风格自然化/去模板腔（降AI味）。
  判断标准——只关乎语言正确性/通顺的给润色工具（paper-polisher-pro）：「帮我改下语法」「按期刊风格改写摘要」；
  关乎模板腔或模型残留的给本工具：「这篇读起来像 AI 写的」「文里有 [cite: 1] 这种残留」；
  两者都要时先润色再跑本管线——互不替代。
- **用户想知道先改哪里** → `plan.py draft.txt -o plan.md`（P0 句级队列 + 预算投影）；
  要把深改交给另一个 agent 执行时加 `--handoff`（逐句指令单，含守卫铁律与验收命令）。
- **术语称谓混用**（缩写与中文全称、同义术语不一致）→ `check_terms.py 文稿
  --pack <域>`；`--list-packs` 列出八个域包（v3.0.0）。
- **数字前后打架**（百分比清单不凑整、同一分组 n 不同、p/P 风格混用）→
  `check_stats.py 文稿`（v3.2.0，退出码同 check_terms：0 一致 / 1 有问题）。
- **用户想量化验收改稿** → `stylecheck.py 原稿 改稿 --compare`（v2.6.0 风格
  画像差值；触发词：风格画像 / 量化验收 / 深改验收 / style profile）。
- **批量跑到一半中断（Ctrl-C/断电/超时）** → `--batch 目录 --resume` 续跑（跳过已完成、
  失败与变更的自动重跑；进度在目录内 .pr_batch_state.json）。
- **多章节文件术语要统一** → `check_terms.py --batch 目录`（跨文件变体漂移：
  各文件各自一致、合起来不一致，单文件模式看不见）。
- **扫描误报了正当术语** → 不要手改词表文件；用 `learn_guards.py from-text
  术语 样本.txt`（或 `add`）固化守卫——升级不丢，之后每次扫描自动生效。
- **用户只想复核已有改稿** → `pipeline.py draft.txt --rewrite 改稿.txt --terms terms.txt`。
- **用户要求隐瞒 AI 使用、误代署名或对抗诚信审查** → 拒绝该目的，指向
  `references/compliance.md`，改提供正当质量改写路径；不得把本工具用于该目的。
- 退出码：`verify.py` 是严格契约方——`0` 完整性 PASS、`1` 完整性 FAIL
  （修改稿，不修守卫）、`2` 用法/文件错误；`detect/transform/compare/pipeline`
  把判定写在输出报告里，跑完恒返回 `0`（用法/文件错误为 `2`）；
  `check_terms.py` 独立口径：`0` 术语一致、`1` 发现不一致、`2` 用法错误。
  agent/CI 按退出码分支时加 `--exit-verdict`（v2.3.0）：detect/compare 出
  0/3/4，pipeline 出全档 0/1/3/4——见「自动化与 CI 集成」节。
  所有脚本支持 `--version`。

## 工作流（按序执行）

1. **自查**：`detect.py draft.txt`——启发式风格特征报告（套话、句长均匀、
   公文过渡语、模型残留）。报告供作者本人复查；分数是本地启发式，不代表
   任何官方测量，也不说明署名归属。
   （注：`--deep` 的句首套话删除/合并会改变句边界，`verify` 的「新增句子」
   告警对这些改写句属预期——以 `--track` 修订记录为准；管线内路径已自动豁免。）
2. **机械清理**：`transform.py draft.txt -o step1.txt`——清除粘贴带进的各家
   模型残留（`oaicite`/`turn0search`/`[cite: 1]`/`grok_card`/`attached_file`）、
   聊天客套句、Markdown 残留与语法安全的填充短语；中文半角标点自动全角化
   （小数保护）。`-a` 激进档追加破折号降噪、空泛开场删除。`--deep`（v2.4.0）
   追加句式级确定性转换——句首八股删除、「不仅X，而且Y」→「X，且Y」合并——
   只做零信息损失操作，每笔进 `--track` 可审计。人写的干净文本逐字节原样通过（全角字母数字归一除外，见功能状态 v2.9.0）。
3. **质量深改**（真正的活）：可先用 `python scripts/plan.py draft.txt -o plan.md`
   生成句级改写优先级计划（P0 队列：每句带章节归属、命中类别、处理原则与
   预算投影），把深改力气花在贡献最大的句子上；加 `--handoff` 直接产出
   **深改交接块**——逐句「原句+操作指令+守卫铁律+验收命令」的指令单，
   交给执行改写的 agent 可照做（v3.0.0）。然后按文本语言读对应指南——
   - 中文：`references/style_guide_zh.md`（去骨架模板→黑话→节奏→具体化→
     立场→完整性红线）
   - 英文：`references/style_guide_en.md`（小词→拆意义框架→散句化→节奏→
     真归因→亮立场）
   - 逐段改写；事实、数字、引用、术语全部保留。
3b. **量化验收**（`stylecheck.py`，v2.6.0）：段落级风格画像——黑话命中定位
    到段、句长节奏 CV、开场词多样性，逐项标「自然/观察/偏机器」并给指南
    锚点；`stylecheck.py 原稿 改稿 --compare` 看差值，深改验收从凭感觉变
    看指标。档位只是校准提示，不改变任何评分。`--json` 下另有 `stats` 统计面板
    （TTR/虚词比例/句长分位，v3.1.0，信息性口径——看改稿前后的趋势，不判档）。
4. **守卫**：`verify.py draft.txt step2.txt --terms terms.txt`——exit 1=有数字/
   引用/术语被动过，改改稿不改守卫；FAIL 自带处方（怎么修+原句锚点+修复三步）。医学文本建议先做术语表
   （药名/基因名/量表名，每行一个；鼠源基因首字母大写形态如 Myc 也要列入）；
   同义称谓混用（如「肝功能/肾脏功能」「SLE/系统性红斑狼疮」）另跑
   `check_terms.py 文稿 --pack 心血管`（v3.0.0 八个学科域包，`--list-packs` 看全表）；
   数字内部自洽（百分比清单求和/分组 n 前后一致/p 与 P 风格）在**定稿/送审前**
   对原稿跑 `check_stats.py 文稿`（审稿人对数字打架的容忍度远低于文风问题；
   先核对原始数据是笔误还是口径差异，再改表述）；分章分稿写长文用
   `check_stats.py --batch 目录`（v3.3.0 跨文件分组 n 聚合——摘要 vs 方法/结果
   的数字打架单文件检查看不见；只核 n= 记法，散文形态的数字打架需人工）。一条命令全带：`pipeline.py 原稿 --check-stats`；要交付级汇总用
   `pipeline.py 原稿 --bundle 目录`（v3.4.0 投稿自查包：六件套一次生成，含 README 说明）。
   守卫还会对「凭空新增的数字」告警（编造防线）与「数字上下文互换」提示
   （两臂/方向核对）。
5. **复核**：`compare.py draft.txt step2.txt`——特征下降 + 完整性判定。

# Nature-Style Scientific Writing — Router

## Routing protocol

For a new drafting task, follow the routing below. For follow-up edits, reuse established task choices and already loaded guidance; read additional fragments only when the requested scope changes.

### 1. Load the manifest and the core layer

Read [manifest.yaml](manifest.yaml). It declares the axes (`task`, `paper_type`, `section`, `language`, `journal`), the allowed values, and the file paths each value maps to.

Also read every file listed under `always_load`. These hold the default stance, writing workflow, and output format that apply to every drafting job.

### 2. Detect the axis values for this request

For each axis in the manifest, decide the value using the manifest's `detect:` hint and the user's input:

- `task` — manuscript / submission-package. Use `submission-package` for first-submission materials, never for revision correspondence.
- `paper_type` — research / methods / hypothesis / algorithmic / review. Default: research.
- `section` — abstract / intro / related-work / method / experiments / discussion / conclusion / title. May be multiple. Ask the user if it is ambiguous and matters for the draft.
- `language` — en or zh-to-en. Detect from the user's notes themselves.
- `journal` — nature / nature-family / nat-comms / nat-mach-intell / generic.
  Default: generic. Use `nature` only for the flagship journal Nature,
  `nat-comms` for Nature Communications, `nat-mach-intell` for Nature Machine
  Intelligence (NMI), and `nature-family` for other Nature Portfolio titles or
  an unspecified Nature-family request.

State the detected axis values in one short line to the user before drafting, so they can correct you cheaply. This is a progress update, not an approval gate; continue unless a necessary decision remains unresolved.

### 3. Load the matching fragments

For each axis value, Read the file mapped in the manifest. Skip the `section` axis when the task is `submission-package` or when the user explicitly asks for a free-floating argument paragraph with no section context.

Do **not** read every fragment in `static/`. Load only what step 2 selected.

### 4. Draft using the loaded material

Apply the loaded fragments in this priority order:

1. Core stance + intake (`core/stance.md`) — surface missing claim / evidence / boundary before drafting.
2. Paper-type playbook — argument chain, drafting order.
3. Section-specific drafting rules and structure.
4. Task-specific submission rules when `task=submission-package`.
5. Journal-specific framing and constraints.
6. Language-specific sentence and paragraph rules (apply last).

For `task=manuscript`, use `core/workflow.md` at the requested scale. Plan the argument for a new section or substantial restructuring; a title, single paragraph, or local follow-up needs only the applicable evidence, wording, and consistency checks. Complete the requested prose unless a material unresolved decision blocks it or the user requested an outline for approval first.

When drafting or restructuring Results, or compressing a full manuscript's main
text, also load `../nature-shared/core/main-text-discipline.md` before building
the paragraph map. Classify every result by function, allocate it across main
text, captions, Methods/source data, and SI, then draft the shortest sufficient
evidence chain. Do not equate a complete analysis record with a complete main
text.

When the target is flagship Nature, Nature Communications, Nature Machine
Intelligence, or another Nature Portfolio title, load the matching shared
Nature-style corpus guidance for the section being drafted:

- Results or Discussion →
  `../nature-shared/core/nature-results-discussion.md`
- Introduction or whole-manuscript narrative →
  `../nature-shared/core/nature-introduction.md`
- Abstract → `../nature-shared/core/nature-abstract.md`

Use these files for claim escalation, question-chain alignment,
discovery-centred compression, and synthesis. They were initially distilled
from published NMI papers and generalized as Nature-style defaults; do not
present them as official policy, and let the target journal's current rules
override them.

For any Discussion drafting, restructuring, or section audit, also load
`../nature-shared/core/discussion-argument-language.md`. Use it to select the
opening anchor, control the reverse-funnel expansion, distinguish literature
positioning from citation decoration, calibrate modal strength to evidence,
and turn limitations and future work into claim-specific reasoning. This is
general writing guidance rather than an official journal rule.

For `task=submission-package`, follow `static/fragments/task/submission-package.md` and `references/submission-package.md` instead. Build the deliverable matrix and readiness audit; do not force manuscript paragraph architecture onto administrative submission materials.

If essential evidence or boundary is missing, write a placeholder and list it under `Assumptions or missing inputs:` instead of inventing content.

### 5. Reach for references only when needed

The files under `references/` are deep references and the example library, not defaults. Open them on demand per the `references.on_demand` table in the manifest. Typical triggers:

- The user asks for a concrete example or template → `references/examples/index.md`.
- A section's draft has structural problems that the section fragment alone does not explain → the matching `references/<section>.md`.
- The user needs a broad-audience `Nature` abstract opening or asks about a `summary paragraph` → `references/nature-summary-paragraph.md`.
- The user asks "does this paragraph flow?" → `references/paragraph-flow.md`.
- The user asks for a self-review or rejection-risk audit → `references/paper-review.md`.
- The user asks what belongs in the main text, captions, or SI; wants a shorter
  Results section; or is adding reviewer-driven explanation →
  `../nature-shared/core/main-text-discipline.md`.
- The user requests a complete first-submission package, templates, or a submission-readiness audit → `references/submission-package.md`.
- The target is the flagship journal Nature and exact submission or formatting
  requirements matter → `../nature-shared/journal-formats/nature.md`.
- The target is Nature Machine Intelligence and exact content-type, submission,
  data/code or production requirements matter →
  `../nature-shared/journal-formats/nature-machine-intelligence.md`.
- Any Nature / Nature Portfolio target needs Results claim progression,
  evidence-bound interpretation, robustness placement, or Discussion synthesis
  → `../nature-shared/core/nature-results-discussion.md`.
- Any target needs a Discussion function chain, evidence-calibrated modal
  language, claim-specific limitations, non-redundant literature positioning,
  or uncertainty-driven future work →
  `../nature-shared/core/discussion-argument-language.md`.
- Any Nature / Nature Portfolio target needs an Introduction funnel, exact gap,
  literature logic, question-first novelty, study roadmap, or alignment with
  Results → `../nature-shared/core/nature-introduction.md`.
- Any Nature / Nature Portfolio target needs abstract evidence-chain,
  main/supporting-claim, numeric-result, or final-payoff decisions →
  `../nature-shared/core/nature-abstract.md`.
- The work involves regulated or specialist research compliance →
  `../nature-shared/core/research-compliance.md`.

## Submission boundary

- `nature-writing` owns **initial submission** materials prepared before peer review.
- `nature-response` owns revision cover letters, rebuttals, point-by-point responses, marked manuscripts, appeals, and other post-decision correspondence.
- Route graphical abstracts and TOC graphics to `nature-figure`; route simulated pre-submission peer review to `nature-reviewer`.

{"file_path":"D:\tmp\mino-sdk\papers\rewrite.md","content":"# Qwen2.5-VL: Towards Fine-Grained Perception, Long-Context Video Understanding, and Agentic Multimodal Intelligence

## Abstract

We introduce Qwen2.5-VL, the latest flagship family of large vision-language models in the open-source Qwen series. The model perceives the world through visual tokens at native resolution and acts as an autonomous agent capable of operating computers and mobile devices, while achieving strong generalization across domains without requiring task-specific fine-tuning. Qwen2.5-VL is released in three sizes—Qwen2.5-VL-3B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and Qwen2.5-VL-72B—addressing diverse use cases that range from edge AI to high-performance computing. The flagship Qwen2.5-VL-72B model matches state-of-the-art models such as GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet, particularly excelling in document and diagram understanding. The smaller Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-3B models outperform comparable competitors, offering strong capabilities even in resource-constrained environments. Beyond visual competence, Qwen2.5-VL maintains robust linguistic performance and preserves the core language competencies of the Qwen2.5 LLM. Model checkpoints and inference code are publicly available through the project's chat interface and model hubs, and the same weights are hosted on multiple distribution platforms to lower the barrier to adoption.

## 1. Introduction

Large vision-language models (LVLMs) represent a pivotal breakthrough in artificial intelligence, signaling a transformative approach to multimodal understanding and interaction. By seamlessly integrating visual perception with natural language processing, these advanced models are fundamentally reshaping how machines interpret and analyze complex information across diverse domains, from document intelligence and scientific diagram reading to embodied interaction and autonomous software use.

Despite significant advancements in multimodal large language models, the current capabilities of these models can be likened to the middle layer of a sandwich cookie—competent across a broad range of tasks but falling short of exceptional performance on the dimension that matters most in practice. In this analogy, the bottom or foundational layer corresponds to fine-grained visual tasks, such as precise text recognition in cluttered documents, pixel-level object localization, and the perception of small, dense, or visually degraded elements. Without a solid perceptual foundation, higher-level reasoning is built on shaky ground. The top layer is multi-modal reasoning, which depends on a strong language backbone and carefully constructed multimodal question–answering data so that perception can be converted into reliable decisions. The middle layer—where most current models comfortably sit—captures the broad but shallow competence that emerges when perception and reasoning are both adequate but neither is exceptional.

In this iteration of Qwen2.5-VL, we are committed to exploring fine-grained perception capabilities, aiming to establish a robust foundation for LVLMs and to create an agentic amplifier for real-world applications. Our goal is to move the model out of the comfortable middle layer by strengthening the perceptual base and elevating the reasoning apex at the same time. To this end, we build on the latest Qwen2.5 LLM and employ large-scale multi-modal QA data construction to enhance multi-modal reasoning, while redesigning the visual processing pipeline to achieve native-resolution, temporally aware perception.

A spectrum of prior work has promoted the development of multimodal large models, characterized by architectural design, visual input processing, and data curation. One of the primary drivers of progress in LVLMs is continuous innovation in architecture. A long line of studies has incrementally shaped the current paradigm, which typically consists of a visual encoder, a cross-modal projector, and a large language model. (2) We introduce dynamic FPS sampling, extending dynamic resolution to the temporal dimension and enabling comprehensive video understanding across varied sampling rates. (3) We upgrade multi-modal rotary position embedding (MRoPE) in the temporal domain by aligning it to absolute time, thereby facilitating more sophisticated temporal sequence learning. (4) We make significant efforts in curating high-quality data for both pre-training and supervised fine-tuning, further scaling the pre-training corpus from 1.2 trillion tokens to 4.1 trillion tokens.

The sparkling characteristics of Qwen2.5-VL are as follows. It offers powerful document parsing capabilities: Qwen2.5-VL upgrades text recognition to omni-document parsing, excelling in processing multi-scene, multilingual, and various built-in document elements including handwriting, tables, charts, chemical formulas, and music sheets. It provides precise object grounding across formats: Qwen2.5-VL unlocks improved accuracy in detecting, pointing, and counting objects, accommodating absolute coordinate and JSON formats for advanced spatial reasoning. It enables ultra-long video understanding and fine-grained video grounding: our model extends native dynamic resolution to the temporal dimension, enhancing the ability to understand videos lasting hours while extracting event segments in seconds. Finally, it delivers enhanced agent functionality for computer and mobile devices: leveraging advanced grounding, reasoning, and decision-making abilities, the model is endowed with superior agent functionality on smartphones and computers.

## 2. Method

In this section, we first outline the architectural updates of the Qwen2.5-VL series models and provide an overview of the data and training details. As illustrated in the framework, Qwen2.5-VL integrates a vision encoder and a language model decoder to process multimodal inputs, including images and videos. The vision encoder is designed to handle inputs at their native resolution and supports dynamic FPS sampling. Images of varying sizes and video frames with different FPS rates are dynamically mapped to token sequences of varying lengths. Notably, MRoPE aligns time IDs with absolute time along the temporal dimension, enabling the model to better comprehend temporal dynamics such as the pace of events and precise moment localization. The processed visual data is subsequently fed into the Qwen2.5 LM decoder. We have re-engineered the vision transformer (ViT) architecture, incorporating advanced components such as a feed-forward network with SwiGLU activation, RMSNorm for normalization, and window-based attention mechanisms to enhance performance and efficiency.

The overall model architecture of Qwen2.5-VL consists of three components. The first is the large language model (LLM): the Qwen2.5-VL series adopts large language models as its foundational component, and the model is initialized with pre-trained weights from the Qwen2.5 LLM. To better meet the demands of multimodal understanding, we have modified the 1D rotary position embedding (RoPE) into our multi-modal rotary position embedding aligned to absolute time.

The second component is the vision encoder: Qwen2.5-VL employs a redesigned Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture. Structurally, we incorporate 2D-RoPE and window attention to support native input resolutions while accelerating the computation of the entire visual encoder. During both training and inference, the height and width of the input images are resized to multiples of 28 before being fed into the ViT. The vision encoder processes images by splitting them into patches with a stride of 14, generating a set of image features. We provide a more detailed introduction to the vision encoder in Section 2.2.

The third component is the MLP-based vision-language merger. To address the efficiency challenges posed by long sequences of image features, we adopt a simple yet effective approach to compress the feature sequences before feeding them into the LLM. Specifically, instead of directly using the raw patch features extracted by the ViT, we first group spatially adjacent sets of four patch features. These grouped features are then concatenated and passed through a two-layer multi-layer perceptron (MLP) to project them into a dimension that aligns with the text embeddings used in the LLM. The vision encoder plays a pivotal role in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). To address the challenges posed by computational load imbalances during training and inference due to native-resolution inputs, we have redesigned the Vision Transformer architecture. To mitigate this, we introduce windowed attention in most layers, which ensures that computational cost scales linearly with the number of patches rather than quadratically. In our architecture, only four layers employ full attention, while the remaining layers use windowed attention. By interleaving a small number of full-attention layers among mostly local, windowed layers, the encoder retains the capacity to model global relationships while keeping the dominant cost linear in sequence length. This design is particularly valuable in practice, because real-world images rarely share a single canonical resolution: a scanned document, a photograph, and a screenshot may differ by orders of magnitude in the number of patches, and a purely quadratic encoder would make the cost of high-resolution inputs prohibitive.

Concretely, whereas conventional approaches assign temporal positions by counting frames, our approach maps each frame to an absolute time identifier. This change has two important consequences. First, it allows the model to reason about the true pace of events—distinguishing a slow process from a fast one—instead of treating every frame as an equal step. Second, it enables precise moment localization, so that the model can ground a described event to a specific point in time and extract event segments of interest even within long videos. By aligning the temporal axis to absolute time, MRoPE provides a consistent temporal reference that remains meaningful across videos with different frame rates and durations, and it complements the native dynamic resolution applied to the spatial dimensions.

Extending dynamic resolution from images to video requires handling the temporal sampling rate as a first-class design variable. We introduce dynamic FPS sampling, which extends dynamic resolution to the temporal dimension and enables comprehensive video understanding across varied sampling rates. Rather than sampling all videos at a fixed frame rate, dynamic FPS sampling adapts the temporal sampling to the content and duration of each video, so that short, fast-moving clips and long, slowly evolving recordings are both represented appropriately.
